gaps.sentence: So convincing ___ his argument that nobody objected.
gaps.explanation: So + adjective at the front: was his argument that…

gaps.sentence: Only when the last vote had been counted ___ the returning officer speak.
gaps.explanation: 'Only when' at the front forces question order: did the returning officer speak.

gaps.sentence: So difficult ___ the exam that half the candidates failed.
gaps.explanation: So difficult was the exam that… — inversion for emphasis.

gaps.sentence: Come ___ it may, the trial must proceed.
gaps.explanation: 'Come what may' — fixed inverted idiom = whatever happens.

gaps.sentence: Not since the winter of 1963 ___ temperatures dropped so low.
gaps.explanation: 'Not since 1963 have temperatures dropped …' — the only time from then until now.

gaps.sentence: ___ the committee reach a decision, we cannot proceed.
gaps.explanation: Fronting 'Until…' emphasises the condition blocking progress.

gaps.sentence: Only later ___ we realise what he had done.
gaps.explanation: 'Only later did we realise' — inverted past simple.

gaps.sentence: Were it not ___ the funding cuts, the library would still be open.
gaps.hint: were it not ___ = if it were not for
gaps.explanation: 'Were it not for' introduces the one thing preventing the outcome.
